summary: A Prompt render case titles a byte-identity with a singleton tick that its body never asserts and that the concurrency line makes false

per.section: A green verdict is proven non-vacuous

acceptance: the case states a claim its body asserts in the stated direction: that an assignedEntry under a phase declining `scopeWritesToEntry` changes no byte of the render, asserted against the same phase rendered without one rather than against a singleton tick the case never builds and could not match — and the parenthetical stops naming an absent assignedEntry the body supplies
pins: a phase that declines scopeWritesToEntry renders the same bytes with an assignedEntry as without one
notes: Verified on disk: `entryWriteScope` (`src/paths.ts:240`) returns `undefined` absent `scopeWritesToEntry`, and is the only path `assignedEntry` takes into `prependHarnessBlock` (`src/Prompt.ts:684`) — so the identity holds and is pinnable. A singleton's render is not byte-identical: `Concurrency:` differs. The phrase is the spec's, about the write allowance (`spec/pending.md:348`), pinned there at `tests/Dispatcher.test.ts:8895`. Test-only diff, so `pins[]` and no `tests[]`.
